scope.notes: Inventory in progress (253 rows). Covers Exalted: The Lunars core innate powers (Lunar Shapechanging, the Tell, True Forms, Caste Mark tattooing/Fixing the Caste, Casteless consequences), the full Shapechanging I/II/III Charm trees (with the Deadly Beastman Transformation gift table), the full Body Enhancement I/II Charm trees, the full Unarmed Combat I through V Charm trees plus three further Body Weapon Technique-rooted utility Charms -- completing the entire Unarmed Combat Charm category -- the complete Melee Combat I/II Charm trees (26 Charms), the complete Ranged Combat I/II Charm trees (17 Charms), pp. 149-161/PDF 152-164, the complete Defensive I/II/III Charm trees (21 Charms), pp. 161-167/PDF 164-170, the complete Survival and Healing I/II/III/IV Charm trees (22 Charms), pp. 168-174/PDF 171-177, the complete Perception I/II/III/IV Charm trees (25 Charms), pp. 174-181/PDF 177-184, the complete Stealth Charm tree (6 Charms), pp. 182-183/PDF 185-186, the complete Interaction and Knowledge I/II/III/IV Charm trees (26 Charms), pp. 183-191/PDF 186-194, and the complete Spirit and Sorcery-access Charms (9 Charms), pp. 191-193/PDF 194-196 -- completing every Charm category in Chapter Five. Chapter Four: Traits (pp. 94-115/PDF 97-118) is now also fully inventoried (24 new rows): the five altered Backgrounds (Artifact, Backing, Followers, Manse, Mentor), the three new Backgrounds (Cult, Heart's Blood, Renown) plus their supporting Regions sidebar, all three player Castes (Full Moon, Changing Moon, No Moon) and the Casteless state, the universal Caste anima-effect grants, the Great Curse (this splat's Limit-Trait analog) and its four Virtue-linked thralls (Curse of the Whipped Dog/Heartless Weasel/Drunken Monkey/Raging Bull), the Lunar Anima Banners visibility table, and the Face/Renown social-rank system (Face Trait ranks Urrach-ya through Shahan-ya, the four-category Renown Trait, and the tlak gaining/losing/respecting-face procedures), plus a short Lunars and Regeneration sidebar. No dedicated Lunar-specific Merits/Flaws subsection exists in this chapter -- confirmed absent, not merely unreviewed. This edition of Exalted: The Lunars has three player Castes (No Moon, Full Moon, Changing Moon) plus Casteless, not the five-Caste structure (adding Waxing/Waning Moon) introduced in later editions. Cross-splat supplements are not yet inventoried.

sources.role: Primary Lunar rules, Charms, Backgrounds, Merits/Flaws, and setting material

rulesNotes: Printed page numbers in this book run 3 less than the PDF page number supplied (PDF page = printed page + 3) for the copy used to build this inventory; both are recorded on every citation.
Lunar Charms use Minimum Attribute (not Minimum Ability) fields, per p. 122 (PDF 125).

A handful of rows in the Unarmed Combat III-V trees have book text that reads awkwardly around botch/infection resolution (Rabid Beast Bite, Grasping Pseudopod Method); paraphrased faithfully but flagged in each row's notes for a closer re-read before promotion. Armor-Rending Claw Fist's mechanics also cut off mid-sentence at the bottom of its rendered page and needs the following page reviewed to complete it.

Melee Combat I/II and Ranged Combat I/II are now complete (pp. 149-161/PDF 152-164). Several Charm descriptions span a page break in the source (stat block/tree diagram on one page, prose continuing on the next); these were transcribed as single continuous Charms with a note on the page split where applicable. Arrow-Shaping Method cross-references Shaping the Once-Living Form (an existing Shapechanging II Charm row) as a co-prerequisite alongside Nature's Harmony Advantage.

Defensive I/II/III are now complete (pp. 161-167/PDF 164-170). The Defensive-III tree diagram (PDF p. 169/printed p. 166) labels one node 'Limb-Shedding Growth', but the Charm's own header and running text (PDF p. 170/printed p. 167) both read 'Limb-Shielding Growth' -- the Charm's own text was trusted per the standing rule to prefer stated Charm text over tree-diagram lettering when they conflict. Pack-Saving Method references a reduced-cost case tied to a Charm named 'Brotherhood of Lake and River' not yet located elsewhere in this book; no crossReferences entry was added for it pending that Charm's discovery.

Survival and Healing I/II/III/IV are now complete (pp. 168-174/PDF 171-177). Unerring Den-Finding Sense's own Prerequisite Charms line lists only Beast Instinct Method even though the Survival and Healing II tree diagram draws it alongside Food-Scenting Method and Water-Providing Technique feeding into Wolf Endurance Method; the Charm's own text was trusted. Bruise-Relief Technique's cost/rate sentence reads redundantly in the source and is flagged in its notes for a closer look before promotion.

Perception I/II/III/IV are now complete (pp. 174-181/PDF 177-184). Heightened (Sense) Method is one three-part Charm (sight; hearing/touch; smell/taste) that the Perception II/III/IV tree diagrams draw as three differently-labeled root nodes; those labels were recorded as aliases on a single inventory row rather than as separate Charms. Ritual of Lunar Stability's stat block Duration (lunar months) and mechanics text (weeks) disagree on units for the same permanent-Essence-scaled figure; transcribed faithfully as printed and flagged in its notes.

Stealth (6 Charms, pp. 182-183/PDF 185-186) and Interaction and Knowledge I/II/III/IV (26 Charms, pp. 183-191/PDF 186-194) are now complete. Locating Pack-Forming Presence and Brotherhood of Lake and River in the Interaction and Knowledge III/IV trees closed out both previously-open co-prerequisite items on Sense-Borrowing Method and Pack-Saving Method; their crossReferences were updated and their notes removed. Several rows in this range flag illustration cut-offs or garbled/redundant source phrasing (Chameleon Skin Disguise, Lion Roar Method, Pack-Calling Cry) that were paraphrased as faithfully as legible but merit a second look before promotion.
Spirit Charms (4 Charms) and Sorcery-access Charms (5 Charms), pp. 191-193/PDF 194-196, are now complete, finishing every Charm category in Chapter Five.

Chapter Four: Traits (pp. 94-115/PDF 97-118) is now fully inventoried (24 new rows). Expanded Backgrounds: Artifact, Backing, Followers, and Manse are altered only in flavor text (disposition calculated, no new dot table); Mentor is altered with a re-flavored 0-5 dot table measuring closeness to the character's Silver Pact elder-mentor rather than the mentor's personal power. New Backgrounds: Cult (p. 98-99/PDF 101-102, dot table only runs 0-4 in the legible render -- no 5-dot line was found and this is flagged for a second look before promotion), Heart's Blood (p. 99-100/PDF 102-103, separate 0-5 dot tables for animal forms and for Heart's Blood (Human)), and Renown (p. 100/PDF 103, grants bonus starting points in the separate Renown Trait; Casteless may not take it) plus the supporting Regions sidebar (p. 101/PDF 104) that guides which animals a Heart's Blood purchase may represent by homeland.

Chapter Four's Castes confirm this edition of Exalted: The Lunars has only three player Castes -- Full Moon (pp. 102-103/PDF 105-106), Changing Moon (pp. 104-105/PDF 107-108), and No Moon (pp. 106-107/PDF 109-110) -- plus the uninitiated Casteless state (p. 108/PDF 111), not the five-Caste structure (adding Waxing/Waning Moon) from later editions; the 'Caste' framing text on p. 109/PDF 112 explicitly says essence is fixed into 'one of the three castes.' The universal Caste anima-effect grants (any Lunar may spend 1 mote for one of five minor Tell/Caste-Mark/anima tricks) are inventoried separately from the Lunar Anima Banners table (p. 110/PDF 113), which lists Tell/anima visibility bands by Peripheral Essence spent in a scene.

The Great Curse (p. 109/PDF 112) is this splat's Limit-Trait analog, triggered by acting against a Lunar's primary Virtue or failing a Willpower roll against full moonlight; its four Virtue-linked inner-beast thralls (Curse of the Whipped Dog/Compassion, Heartless Weasel/Conviction, Drunken Monkey/Temperance, Raging Bull/Valor, pp. 109-110/PDF 112-113) were each inventoried as their own row.

The Face/Renown social-rank system (pp. 111-115/PDF 114-118) was inventoried as three rows: the Face Trait itself (six named ranks, Urrach-ya through Shahan-ya, plus the Face Requirements table of minimum Renown and other prerequisites per rank), the four-category Renown Trait (Succor/Compassion, Mettle/Conviction, Cunning/Temperance, Glory/Valor -- distinct from the Renown Background, which merely grants bonus starting points toward it), and the tlak ceremony/losing-face/respecting-face social procedures. A short Lunars and Regeneration sidebar (p. 115/PDF 118) closes out the chapter, cross-referenced to the existing Deadly Beastman Transformation and Halting the Scarlet Flow Charm rows.

No dedicated Lunar-specific Merits/Flaws subsection was found anywhere in Chapter Four; the chapter moves directly from New Backgrounds into Castes/Great Curse/Face without one. This is confirmed absent, not merely unreviewed -- the chapter's opening statement says Merits/Flaws otherwise work identically to core Exalted. Likewise, no dedicated Tribe write-up or Tribe-as-Background section exists; Lunar tribes are addressed only through the altered Backing/Followers text and general chapter flavor, not as a discrete character-creation mechanic.

Chapter Four: Traits is now fully inventoried, completing every planned item in the Lunar intake scope drawn from the primary sourcebook. Remaining outstanding work is limited to the untriaged cross-splat supplements (Blood and Salt, Book of Bone and Ebony, Savage Seas, etc.) listed in the top-level intent; see docs/references/exalted1e/lunar/README.md.
